title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, assembled from the surrounding pages:
- M is a set of elementary pieces (cells) with an order ≤ and a refinement/domination relation ≪.
- Two pieces can be 'compatible' and 'disjoint'.
- A 'figure' F ⊂ M is a family of mutually compatible pieces.
- Each piece X has a set of 'lieux' (loci) X̃, with an 'interior' X̃°. The 'ombre' (shadow) F̃ of F is the union of the loci of its members.
- A 'contrée' (region) is a subset of M stable under passing to smaller/refining pieces: a down-set or sieve for ≪.
- Cond 5 (p. 39) says disjointness is inherited by refinements.

This page introduces the region calculus attached to figures.

(1) Induced region C_F. This is the set of X ∈ M that refine F, i.e. the sieve generated by (dominated by) F. The margin NB relates the loci of C_F to the shadow of F.

(2) Residual region C_{∁F}. This is the set of X ∈ M disjoint from F. By Cond 5 it is again a region (stable under ≪). The margin attempts to describe its loci: the loci disjoint from F, which are not simply the complement of the shadow.

(3) Relative residual region of F inside G. It is defined as an intersection of an induced region with a residual one. The intended meaning is surely C_G ∩ C_{∁F}: the pieces refining G and disjoint from F. The handwriting shows overwritten subscripts.

(4) Subdivision. A subdivision of a figure F is a figure F' ⊂ M that (a) refines F and (b) is maximal among figures refining F.

(5) NB. If F' refines F, then the shadow of F' is contained in the shadow of F.

Purpose. The next page proves that F' is a subdivision iff no piece refining F is disjoint from F'. Equivalently, every locus of F̃ compatible with all of F̃' already lies in F̃'. That direction needs a new axiom (Cond 7: interiors of distinct pieces are disjoint).

In modern terms:
- C_F is the principal sieve / down-set generated by F.
- C_{∁F} is the pseudo-complement ¬C_F in the Heyting algebra of sieves (as for open sets of a locale, or sieves in a presheaf topos).
- A subdivision is a refinement that is ¬¬-dense in C_F.

This is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs' (tame topology): polyhedra-like 'figures' made of cells, with subdivision characterised order-theoretically rather than via point-set topology.
errors: 'Par Constr. 5' should read 'Cond 5' (the condition stated on p. 39).

Gap: Cond 5 as stated concerns X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y simultaneously. Deducing that C_{∁F} is stable under ≪ (keeping Y ∈ F fixed) requires ≪ to be reflexive, or a one-sided version of Cond 5. With a strict way-below-type relation the argument does not directly apply.
The relative residual region is written ambiguously ('C_F ∩ C_{∁G}' with overwritten subscripts). For 'residual region of F in G' the coherent formula is C_G ∩ C_{∁F}.

Existence of a subdivision (a maximal figure refining F) is not justified. It needs a finiteness hypothesis or Zorn's lemma plus closure of figures under unions of chains. Uniqueness is neither claimed nor true in general.
The margin assertion identifying the loci of C_F with the shadow of F is only tentative (partly illegible). It presumably requires further axioms relating loci to pieces.

ideas.what: Induced region C_F: the set of pieces refining a figure F
ideas.modern_name: principal sieve / down-set generated by a subset in a poset; open set of an Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard order theory; sieves in Grothendieck topologies (SGA 4)
ideas.where_published: sieve language in SGA 4, but not this specific analysis-situs setup

ideas.what: Residual region C_{∁F}: pieces disjoint from F, a region by Cond 5
ideas.modern_name: pseudo-complement ¬U in the Heyting algebra of sieves/opens
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heyting algebras, Stone; locale theory (Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone)

ideas.what: Subdivision of a figure as a maximal refining figure, later characterised as one with no piece disjoint from it (p. 41)
ideas.modern_name: dense (¬¬-dense) refinement; maximal antichain-type covering; combinatorial subdivision in PL topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology (subdivisions of complexes); density/double negation topology (Lawvere–Tierney)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this axiomatic treatment is unpublished

ideas.what: Shadow monotonicity: a refinement's shadow lies in the original's shadow

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic, point-free 'analysis situs'. Pieces with a refinement relation, figures, shadows of loci, regions as sieves, residual regions as pseudo-complements, and subdivisions as maximal (dense) refinements form a combinatorial foundation for tame topology. This is distinct from o-minimality and from locale theory, though structurally close to both. The programme was not pursued in the literature.
missed.quote: On appelle subdivision de F une figure F' ⊂ M telle que a) F' soit un raffinement de F b) F' soit maximale, parmi les figures qui raffinent F.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an order-theoretic/point-free formulation of PL-type subdivision that could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions and with locale-theoretic density. It is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to realise the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse.

missed.claim: Taken with p. 41, the residual-region and subdivision definitions identify subdivisions with ¬¬-dense refinements in the Heyting algebra of regions. This links Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics to the double-negation (dense) topology of topos theory, a link he does not state explicitly.
missed.quote: La contrée résiduelle d'une figure F dans G est par définition C_F ∩ C_{CG}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a topos-theoretic/locale reading of tame topology, where subdivision invariance corresponds to working in a ¬¬-sheaf subtopos.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions themselves are elementary order theory. They are part of a little-known, unpublished 1986 axiomatic attempt at tame topology/analysis situs, which is of historical interest, but the page contains no deep result.
transcription_corrections: 'Par Constr. 5' in the image is most likely 'Par Cond. 5', referring to the condition of p. 39.
The final formula's subscripts are overwritten. It likely reads C_G ∩ C_{∁F} or a corrected variant, not unambiguously C_F ∩ C_{CG}.
In 1°), the crossed-out phrase is 'définie par les'. Above C_F, 'induite' is inserted.
In the subdivision definition, '⊂ M' is inserted above 'une figure' ('Soit F ⊂ M figure, et G'), and the clause is 'On appelle subdivision de F une figure F' ⊂ M telle que'.
In clause a), 'par C' is an inserted annotation below 'raffinement de F'.
In the final NB, the shadow notation is a tilde (F̃', F̃), consistent with the next page, not a bar.
